task: Edit this longer fictional adapted news feature into about 350–500 words. Preserve its route-specific explanation, useful advice from the publisher, and distinct print and PDF correction plans. Credit the original reporting organisation and attribute its reproduced publisher statement accurately; remove invented local reporting, motive, completion, and whole-guide verification claims. The local newsletter has permission to adapt the source, not a record of conducting its own investigation. Do not collapse the useful explanatory feature into a short correction notice.
input:
Our investigation has exposed deliberate deception in the walking guide. We interviewed its authors and discovered that Harbour Lane names two different paths. Following our findings, the guide has already been corrected everywhere. This exclusive report is the work of our newsroom, which has now verified every route in the publication.

The ambiguity concerns two entries with different endpoints. On page 6, the eastern Harbour Lane runs from the station to the canal. On page 18, the western Harbour Lane runs from the park to the ferry ramp. The entries belong to separate sections, Station Walk and Waterside Circuit, rather than describing opposite ends of a single continuous lane.

The maps already give the routes different codes: E2 for the eastern entry and W4 for the western one. That extra information matters when a direction is copied without its surrounding page. A lane name alone does not tell the reader which of these entries is intended. Keeping the code with the name preserves a distinction that the full guide contains but an isolated instruction can lose.

The publisher told us, "For now, use the route code as well as the lane name." It plans to label the entries Harbour Lane (East) and Harbour Lane (West) in the next edition. The proposed qualifiers change the guide's labels, not the official names of streets. The described routes and endpoints are not being changed by this editorial correction.

The downloadable PDF is a separate part of the plan. The publisher intends to add a clarification to the current PDF before the next printed edition, although neither release date has been set. Printed copies of the current edition remain in circulation. No recall or free-replacement arrangement has been announced, so readers should not assume that owning the guide will automatically bring a new copy through the post.

The available comparison covers these two entries. It supplies no count of complaints or evidence that anyone was injured or stranded. The duplicate name calls for a precise clarification, but it does not by itself explain how the wording arose. Readers need the corrected distinction and the status of each publication format, not speculation about the motives of the people who compiled the guide.
